Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that streams microphone audio and yields interim transcripts using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 4 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 5 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 6 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
import logging
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from deepgram import (
    DeepgramClient,
    LiveTranscriptionEvents,
    LiveOptions,
    Microphone,
)

load_dotenv()

# Set up logging to show informational messages.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

async def stream_transcription() -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]:
    """
    Streams microphone audio and yields interim transcripts using Deepgram.

    This function sets up a connection to Deepgram's streaming API,
    captures audio from the microphone, and yields transcription results
    as they are received.
    """
    transcript_queue: asyncio.Queue[str | None] = asyncio.Queue()
    dg_connection = None
    microphone = None

    try:
        # Create a Deepgram client using the API key from environment variables.
        # The DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable is required.
        deepgram = DeepgramClient()

        # Create a connection to Deepgram's streaming endpoint.
        dg_connection = deepgram.listen.asynclive.v("1")

        # Define event handlers for the connection.
        async def on_message(self, result, **kwargs):
            """Handle received transcription results."""
            sentence = result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript
            if result.is_final and len(sentence.strip()) > 0:
                logging.info(f"Final transcript: '{sentence}'")
            if not result.is_final and len(sentence) > 0:
                await transcript_queue.put(sentence)

        async def on_error(self, error, **kwargs):
            """Handle connection errors."""
            logging.error(f"Deepgram connection error: {error}")
            await transcript_queue.put(None)  # Signal termination

        async def on_close(self, **kwargs):
            """Handle connection closure."""
            logging.info("Deepgram connection closed.")
            await transcript_queue.put(None)  # Signal termination


        # Register the event handlers.
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Transcript, on_message)
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Error, on_error)
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Close, on_close)

        # Configure the transcription options.
        # interim_results=True allows us to get partial transcripts.
        options = LiveOptions(
            model="nova-2",
            language="en-US",
            smart_format=True,
            interim_results=True,
        )

        # Start the connection.
        await dg_connection.start(options)

        # Create and start the microphone stream.
        microphone = Microphone(dg_connection.send)
        microphone.start()
        logging.info("Microphone started. Speak now.")

        # Yield transcripts from the queue as they arrive.
        while True:
            transcript = await transcript_queue.get()
            if transcript is None:
                break
            yield transcript

    except Exception as e:
        logging.error(f"An unexpected error occurred: {e}")
    finally:
        # Clean up resources.
        if microphone and microphone.is_active():
            microphone.finish()
        if dg_connection and dg_connection.is_connected():
            await dg_connection.finish()
        logging.info("Transcription stream finished.")
